knowledge:
- key_parameters: groups=Factor vector specifying the group/class of each sample in the training set ;; nTop=Number of top up-regulated genes to include in the signature ;; nBottom=Number of top down-regulated genes to include in the signature ;; alpha=Significance threshold for feature selection (p-value cutoff) ;; N=Fraction of edges (quantile of distances) to keep in the network
- alternatives: Cytoscape (via scudoCytoscape) can be used for network visualization instead of R's scudoPlot. igraph community detection algorithms (like cluster_spinglass) can be used for unsupervised clustering of the network.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing gene expression profiles (microarray or RNA-seq) to identify robust, rank-based transcriptional signatures for sample classification, diagnostic modeling, or network-based sample clustering.
- pitfalls: Feature selection represents a performance bottleneck during cross-validation; the documentation recommends performing feature selection/filtering before running caret cross-validation to speed up the process. Cytoscape must be open when running scudoCytoscape.

workflows.name: unsupervised_network_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify sample-specific signatures, construct similarity networks, and cluster samples.
workflows.stages: 1. Train SCUDO model and extract signatures using scudoTrain ;; 2. Inspect signatures using upSignatures and consensusUpSignatures ;; 3. Generate sample network using scudoNetwork ;; 4. Visualize network using scudoPlot or scudoCytoscape ;; 5. Analyze test set using scudoTest ;; 6. Cluster network using igraph::cluster_spinglass
workflows.code:
trainRes <- scudoTrain(trainData, groups = bt[inTrain], nTop = 100,
    nBottom = 100, alpha = 0.1)
trainRes

upSignatures(trainRes)[1:5,1:5]
consensusUpSignatures(trainRes)[1:5, ]

trainNet <- scudoNetwork(trainRes, N = 0.25)
scudoPlot(trainNet, vertex.label = NA)

# scudoCytoscape(trainNet)

testRes <- scudoTest(trainRes, testData, bt[-inTrain], nTop = 100,
    nBottom = 100)
testRes

testNet <- scudoNetwork(testRes, N = 0.25)
scudoPlot(testNet, vertex.label = NA)

testClust <- igraph::cluster_spinglass(testNet, spins = 2)
plot(testClust, testNet, vertex.label = NA)

workflows.name: supervised_classification_with_tuning
workflows.intent: Perform supervised classification of test samples with hyperparameter tuning via caret.
workflows.stages: 1. Perform pre-filtering/feature selection using Kruskal-Wallis test to avoid caret bottlenecks ;; 2. Define parameter search grid using scudoModel ;; 3. Run cross-validation using caret::train ;; 4. Classify test samples using scudoClassify with the best tuned parameters ;; 5. Evaluate classification performance using caret::confusionMatrix
workflows.code:
classRes <- scudoClassify(trainData, testData, N = 0.25, nTop = 100,
    nBottom = 100, trainGroups = bt[inTrain], alpha = 0.1)

caret::confusionMatrix(classRes$predicted, bt[-inTrain])

trainData <- exprs(ALLB[, inTrain])
virtControl <- rowMeans(trainData)
trainDataNorm <- trainData / virtControl
pVals <- apply(trainDataNorm, 1, function(x) {
    stats::kruskal.test(x, stage[inTrain])$p.value})
trainDataNorm <- t(trainDataNorm[pVals <= 0.01, ])

cl <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(2)
doParallel::registerDoParallel(cl)

model <- scudoModel(nTop = (2:6)*20, nBottom = (2:6)*20, N = 0.25)
control <- caret::trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5,
    summaryFunction = caret::multiClassSummary)
cvRes <- caret::train(x = trainDataNorm, y = stage[inTrain], method = model,
    trControl = control)

parallel::stopCluster(cl)

classStage <- scudoClassify(ALLB[, inTrain], ALLB[, -inTrain], 0.25,
    cvRes$bestTune$nTop, cvRes$bestTune$nBottom, stage[inTrain], alpha = 0.01)
caret::confusionMatrix(classStage$predicted, stage[-inTrain])
